quizzes.title: Module 1 Quiz: Starting Out as an E-commerce VA

questions.text: What does an E-commerce VA primarily do?
choices: Manages an online store's listings, orders, and customer service remotely
Handles a company's payroll
Repairs computer hardware
Manages warehouse construction

questions.text: Why do most online sellers hire an E-commerce VA?
choices: They are legally required to
Running a store's daily tasks becomes more than they can handle alone
It is cheaper than hiring no one
Online stores require a license to operate

questions.text: Which store model gives the seller their own independent, branded website?
choices: Amazon
Shopify
Etsy only
None of these

questions.text: What best describes Amazon as a selling platform?
choices: A marketplace with huge built-in traffic and strict seller rules
A tool only for email marketing
A free website builder with no rules
A platform exclusively for handmade goods

questions.text: What is a key part of setting up a productive home workspace for e-commerce work?
choices: A reliable internet connection and an organized file system
Working only from a phone with no backup plan
Avoiding all spreadsheets
Sharing your client login with friends

questions.text: In dropshipping, who typically ships the product to the customer?
choices: A third-party supplier, not the seller directly
The seller always ships it personally
The customer picks it up in person
It is never actually shipped

questions.text: What best describes social commerce?
choices: Buying happens directly inside a social media app like TikTok
A type of in-store cash register
A method of paying employees
A way to remove products from a store

questions.text: What generally affects how much an E-commerce VA can charge?
choices: Platform depth, scope of work, and portfolio strength
The VA’s favorite color
The time zone of the client only
Nothing - all E-commerce VAs charge the same rate

questions.text: Where does a Shopify VA go to manage orders and mark them fulfilled?
choices: The Orders tab in the Shopify admin
A separate accounting app only
Amazon Seller Central
A personal email inbox

questions.text: What is the difference between FBA and FBM on Amazon?
choices: FBA means Amazon stores and ships the product; FBM means the seller does
FBA and FBM are the same thing
FBM is only for digital products
FBA means the seller ships internationally only

questions.text: Why does Amazon require a white background for main product images?
choices: It's one of Amazon's listing image requirements for consistency
It makes photos load faster
It is optional and rarely followed
It only applies to clothing items

questions.text: What is a key purpose of tools like Sellbrite or Linnworks?
choices: Designing company logos
Syncing inventory across multiple sales channels to prevent overselling
Processing payroll
Writing product descriptions automatically

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a helpdesk tool like Gorgias or Zendesk?
choices: Organizing customer messages into tickets so nothing gets lost
Tracking company payroll
Hosting product photos
Managing supplier contracts

questions.text: Why is monitoring Amazon account health metrics important?
choices: Poor metrics like late shipment rate can lead to account suspension
Metrics have no effect on a seller account
It is only relevant for FBA sellers
It replaces the need for customer service

questions.text: Which tool is commonly used for removing a product photo's background?
choices: Remove.bg
QuickBooks
Trello
Zendesk

questions.text: What is a key feature of TikTok Shop for sellers?
choices: Products can be tagged directly in short videos or livestreams
It only supports print catalogs
It requires no fulfillment at all
It cannot be used by affiliates or creators

questions.text: What should you do before running a large bulk product upload?
choices: Test the template with just a few products first
Skip reviewing the results afterward
Delete the original file immediately
Avoid using the platform’s official template

questions.text: What does a seller pay for with Amazon PPC (Sponsored Products)?
choices: A charge each time a shopper clicks the ad
A flat yearly licensing fee
Nothing - Amazon PPC is entirely free
A charge only when the item is out of stock

questions.text: What is the difference between a feature and a benefit in a product listing?
choices: A feature is what the product has; a benefit explains why that matters to the buyer
They mean exactly the same thing
A benefit is only used in Amazon listings
A feature always comes after the benefit

questions.text: What is the correct order in a typical order fulfillment workflow?
choices: Order and payment confirm, item is picked/packed/shipped, tracking is added
Tracking is added before the order is placed
The customer ships the item back first
Payment is confirmed after the item is delivered

questions.text: Why is it important to update tracking numbers immediately after shipping?
choices: It has no real effect on the customer
Missing or wrong tracking is a common cause of customer support tickets
Carriers require it to process the payment
It is only needed for international orders

questions.text: How should an E-commerce VA handle an upset customer?
choices: Argue about who is at fault
Acknowledge their frustration and focus on the solution
Ignore the message
Immediately issue a refund without checking the policy

questions.text: Why should return reasons be logged and shared with the client?
choices: They have no use once a refund is processed
Patterns in returns can reveal a product or listing problem worth fixing
It is only required for accounting purposes
It replaces the need for customer communication

questions.text: What is the recommended way to respond to a negative product review?
choices: Respond calmly, never defensively, and offer to resolve it
Delete it without responding
Argue publicly with the reviewer
Offer payment in exchange for changing the review

questions.text: What is a chargeback?
choices: A customer disputes a charge directly through their bank or card
A discount code applied at checkout
A type of product return label
A fee charged for using a coupon

questions.text: What is the difference between cross-selling and upselling?
choices: Cross-selling suggests a related item; upselling suggests a better/bigger version of the same item
They are exactly the same technique
Cross-selling only applies to refunds
Upselling means offering a lower price

questions.text: What is a 'mock listing' used for in a portfolio?
choices: A real paid client project
A sample listing created to demonstrate your skills
A type of scam
A required legal document

questions.text: How should mock listings be labeled in a portfolio?
choices: As real client results with no disclaimer
Clearly and honestly as sample or practice work
They should never be shown
As guaranteed sales outcomes for future clients

questions.text: What is a good way to showcase improvements in a portfolio?
choices: Vague claims with no specifics
Clear before/after examples of listings or store changes
Only screenshots of unrelated websites
Avoiding results entirely

questions.text: Which free tools work well for building a simple portfolio page?
choices: Canva, Google Sites, or Carrd
Only expensive custom-built websites
None exist for free
Only printed paper portfolios

questions.text: Why is a portfolio valuable even without paid e-commerce client experience?
choices: It has no real value
It proves your skills with listings, photo editing, and organization
It replaces the need for any actual skills
Clients never look at portfolios

questions.text: What should a mock store audit in your portfolio include?
choices: A few observations plus specific, actionable recommendations
Only vague, general compliments about the store
Private customer data from the store
Nothing - audits should never be shown to clients

questions.text: What is a good use for a short portfolio walkthrough video?
choices: Showing your voice and communication style beyond a static resume
Replacing the need for any written portfolio at all
Sharing a client’s private login information
Avoiding the need to ever apply to jobs

questions.text: What makes a client testimonial strong?
choices: It names a specific result, not just a vague compliment
It is written entirely by the VA, not the client
It never mentions any actual outcome
It must always be anonymous

questions.text: What should an E-commerce VA resume bullet point focus on?
choices: Vague statements with no detail
Specific results and tasks, with numbers when possible
Only job titles
Personal hobbies unrelated to the role

questions.text: What makes a strong proposal for an e-commerce job posting?
choices: A generic copy-paste message sent to everyone
Personalization that references the client's actual store and needs
Extremely long, unfocused paragraphs
No mention of relevant platforms or tools

questions.text: Which platforms are commonly used to find E-commerce VA clients?
choices: OnlineJobs.ph and Upwork
Only local newspapers
Random unrelated apps
None, clients cannot be found online

questions.text: What is a good goal during a discovery call with a potential client?
choices: Avoid asking any questions
Understand the client's store, goals, and expectations
Immediately demand payment before speaking
Refuse to discuss the client's products

questions.text: A good freelance profile headline for an E-commerce VA should be:
choices: Vague, like 'Hardworking VA'
Specific and benefit-driven, naming the platforms and value you offer
Left blank
Written only in technical jargon

questions.text: How should you approach a paid trial task from a potential client?
choices: Treat it with the same care as real paid work
Rush through it without reading the instructions
Ignore any clarifying questions you might have
Refuse to complete any trial tasks ever

questions.text: What is a smart way to negotiate without undervaluing yourself?
choices: Offer a smaller scope instead of simply lowering your rate
Always agree to whatever rate is offered
Refuse to discuss scope at all
Never put any agreement in writing

questions.text: Which is a red flag to watch for in a client job posting?
choices: Vague scope paired with an unrealistically low budget
A clearly defined scope and fair budget
A client who answers questions patiently
A reasonable, agreed-upon timeline

quizzes.title: Module 6 Quiz: Landing Your First Client and Beyond

questions.text: What is a good first step when onboarding a new e-commerce client?
choices: Guess what they want without asking
Clarify goals, access needs, and priority tasks in writing
Immediately increase your rate
Avoid all communication in week one

questions.text: Which is a common pricing model for E-commerce VA services?
choices: Monthly retainer
Random guessing
Refusing to state a price
Charging only in a currency you don't understand

questions.text: What is a practical way to manage multiple client stores without mixing them up?
choices: Use one shared login for every client
Use separate trackers and clearly labeled folders per client
Post the same listings to every client's store
Avoid using any organizational tools

questions.text: How should an E-commerce VA respond to difficult client feedback?
choices: Take it personally and stop responding
Listen professionally, clarify the concern, and revise where reasonable
Argue that the client is always wrong
Ignore the feedback completely

questions.text: What helps build a long-term E-commerce VA career?
choices: Refusing to learn new platforms or tools
Asking for testimonials and continuously learning new platform features
Never asking for client feedback
Avoiding all specialization

questions.text: Why should account access be given through a staff/collaborator role rather than a shared password?
choices: It's safer and keeps the client as the true account owner
It gives the VA full ownership of the store
Platforms don't allow staff accounts
It has no security benefit

questions.text: What is a healthy way to handle reaching client capacity?
choices: Keep adding clients even if quality slips
Pause new clients or raise rates instead of stretching too thin
Stop tracking hours entirely
Lower your rates to attract more clients

questions.text: What does DDP mean in international shipping?
choices: The seller covers duties and taxes upfront for the customer
The customer always pays duties on delivery
The product cannot be shipped internationally
Duties are never charged on any order

questions.text: What does COGS stand for, and why does it matter?
choices: Cost of Goods Sold - it helps show a rough profit picture
Customer Order Growth Score - a marketing metric only
A shipping carrier abbreviation
A type of product return policy

questions.text: What is the main benefit of writing SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures)?
choices: They turn a known task into a repeatable process others can follow
They are required by law for every online store
They replace the need for any client communication
They only apply to Amazon sellers
